newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $0.50-trade.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $0.50-trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices on Wednesday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, pressured by large hog marketings on Tuesday and outlooks for continued hefty movement on Wednesday, livestock dealers said.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hog marketings were estimated at 110,000 head, which several dealers said most likely was met. Monday's actual receipts of 100,000 head matched that day's estimate, USDA reported.
Hog producers slowed marketings since late last week when prices soared on news Tawian had suspended pork shipments becasue of foot and mouth disease in its hog herd.
The suspension fueled steep advances in CME pork complex futures and cash hog prices amid perceptions that Japan would buy more U.S. pork to replace supplies from Taiwan.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs at the plant could range $51.00 to $51.50. The top price on Tuesday was $51.50, up $4.00 since the news of Taiwan's pork suspensions was announced overnight Wednesday.
Illinois top prices at the plant could range $51.00 to $51.50 and Indiana/Ohio top prices for hogs delivered to the plant could span $50.00 to $50.50.
